solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Intense fellow that is rector with Anglicans

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is
CE, the Church of England, is the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A passionate man who is a parish rector among the Anglican faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce heat or fierce competition is intense, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Notes tip for mobilising — get going!

indicators.note: mobilising sets things moving, so the letters of the two words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A tip passed on in written notes about mobilising troops, ending with an order to move.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal imperative urging someone to hurry, the same as telling them to get going.

clue.text: Stage suppressing a noise by crew for megastar?

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so the stage word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
din means a loud noise
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A theatre stage drowning out a crew's racket, and a question about who the star is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks theatrical, but here it is a leg of a journey; 'by' just places the crew word next to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male actor in a film or play is its star, here inflated to megastar with a question mark.

clue.text: Favour element without Republican

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for the party member is taken out of the element

parts.note: boron is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A political favour granted when the Republican element is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from BORON gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or favour asked or granted, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rule facing drivers left in M1 despite getting diverted

indicators.note: traffic being diverted takes a new route, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the motorway name is read as the letters M and I, the figure 1 standing for I

explanation.surface: Motorists stuck on Britain's M1 motorway despite being diverted, and the road rule they face.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A maximum permitted speed is a regulation every motorist must obey on the road.

clue.text: Go crazy after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone going mad after a political revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: have a go, an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a go at it, an attempt.

clue.text: A queen entertaining minute for fashion designer

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so the queen holds the letter for minute

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A queen hosting a fashion designer for a brief visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is the celebrated Italian couturier who founded the fashion house of that name.

clue.text: Nancy's parting shot?

parts.note: Nancy is a city in France, so its parting words would be French ones meaning see you soon

explanation.surface: A woman named Nancy delivering a final cutting remark as she leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy reads as a woman's name, but it is the French city, so the farewell is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A French farewell meaning see you soon, which is what someone from that French city might say on leaving.

clue.text: Unit hopes to reform amid trouble

indicators.note: reforming a unit means forming it again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military unit hoping to regroup in the middle of difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in a mess or in difficulty, so it matches being amid trouble.

clue.text: First signs of this heart regularly offering better pulse

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following five words is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor's remark that a steadily beating heart is a good sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a rhythmic beat, and to throb is to beat in that way; as nouns they are synonyms.

clue.text: Nationalist after turbulent period reluctantly enlisted

indicators.note: turbulent means disordered, so the letters of period are thrown about

explanation.surface: A nationalist, after a period of unrest, signing up for the army against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone roped in has been persuaded to take part against their inclination, recruited reluctantly.

clue.text: Adopt host shortly retaining support

indicators.note: retaining means keeping hold of, so the shortened host word holds the support inside
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the host word is dropped

parts.note: an emcee is the host or master of ceremonies at an event
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A host quickly agreeing to take on a supporting cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last E of EMCEE leaves EMCE, which holds BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea is to take it up willingly, the same as adopting it.

clue.text: Magnate once guarded a very long time

indicators.note: guarded means kept inside, so the letters lie within the two words

explanation.surface: A tycoon who once kept watch for an age.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immeasurably long age, a period of very many years.

clue.text: Dislike purpose in embroidery

parts.note: needle is hostility or antagonism, as in a needle match
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes having any purpose in their needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlework on canvas worked in small stitches is a type of embroidery.

clue.text: First person, we hear, against diplomatic work has direct observation?

indicators.note: we hear marks a word heard rather than read, so the pronoun is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
con means against, as in pros and cons
tact is the skill of diplomacy

explanation.surface: A diplomat claims their delicate work involves watching things first hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people looking straight at each other's eyes is a kind of direct looking, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Commit businessman over fee in kennels?

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, so the businessman word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, a businessman
the charge for boarding an animal in kennels could be called a pet rate

explanation.surface: A businessman taking on a fee for keeping his dog in kennels.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime is to commit it.

clue.text: Carry money as a token

parts.note: to tote is to carry

explanation.surface: Carrying some cash as a small gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol, so a token in the sense of sign.

clue.text: Annoying failure first covered up in magazine

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the magazine title

parts.note: Time is a news magazine

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the shortened failure word is reversed
covering the first letter hides it, so it is dropped

parts.note: a loser is a failure

explanation.surface: A tiresome failure first hushed up in a magazine story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first covered' hides the opening letter of the failure word, leaving OSER, and 'up' turns that to RESO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is wearisome and irritating, so annoying.

clue.text: Regularly reclimb tree

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep climbing a tree again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a common deciduous tree.

clue.text: Brief recall of grandfather, maybe

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a grandfather clock is one example of a timer

explanation.surface: A short memory of an elderly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is the noun, a set of instructions; the grandfather is a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of responsibility given to someone, their brief.

clue.text: Strong Greek character on cliff round middle of July

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the cliff word goes around the middle letters

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the month name are taken

explanation.surface: A powerful Greek figure perched on a cliff in midsummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular means brawny and powerful, so strong.

clue.text: Examine in advance park relaid in Troon close to course

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park

indicators.note: relaid means laid out again, so the letters are rearranged
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A park being relaid in Troon near the golf course, inspected beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: Troon is a Scottish seaside town famous for its golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconnoitre is to survey ground before acting, examining it in advance.

clue.text: Impose fee on one in custody

definitions.meaning: to ask a customer for a sum of money as payment
a ward or person placed in someone's care

explanation.surface: Fining a prisoner held in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is billing someone for a service; the other is a person entrusted to one's care.

clue.text: Father clipped gentleman

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father with a neat haircut who is a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used to address a man respectfully, or a knight; a polite term for a gentleman.

clue.text: Hot period I relish initially after turn in ME capital

indicators.note: after a turn the sequence faces the other way, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a day is a period of time

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A hot spell that I enjoy, first of all after a trip to the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is short for Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia in the Middle East.

clue.text: Remain for example to absorb tense place

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it in, so the example word holds the tense letter

parts.note: say is used to mean for example
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay in place while soaking up a tense atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is not to move from where one is, so to remain.

clue.text: Select film that's mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the word for film is heard rather than seen

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Choosing a movie that someone has recommended.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to choose, a plain synonym of select.

clue.text: Lead singer, one in distant orbit?

definitions.meaning: Freddie of that surname fronted the band Queen
a planet circling the Sun, far away from us

explanation.surface: A rock frontman whose career has taken him into the stratosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Mercury was Queen's frontman, and Mercury is also the planet nearest the Sun.

clue.text: Handle roughly scholar and university lecturer

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: An academic and a university lecturer roughing someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To maul is to treat savagely or batter, so to handle roughly.

clue.text: Superb trio from the East by college

parts.note: the Magi were the three wise men who came from the East

explanation.surface: A wonderful trio of Eastern visitors at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic as an informal adjective means wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Elevated club, maybe, to seek character

parts.note: to court favour is to seek it
a card is an eccentric person, a character

explanation.surface: A grand golf club seeking members of good character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'club' is a playing-card suit, not a golf or social club.
explanation.definitionFit: A king, queen or jack of clubs is a high-ranking court card, one example of the type.
